name: love is respect
summary: Support for young people experiencing dating abuse or unhealthy relationship patterns.

sections.title: About love is respect
sections.text: love is respect is a national resource specifically for young people ages 12-24 who are experiencing dating abuse, curious about healthy relationships, or concerned about a friend. A project of the National Domestic Violence Hotline, love is respect offers 24/7 confidential support through phone, text, and online chat. The organization provides young people with the information, tools, and support they need to recognize and navigate the complexities of dating relationships and identify early warning signs of abuse.

sections.title: How to Reach love is respect
sections.text: Call 1-866-331-9474 any time, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Text LOVEIS to 22522 for support via text message. Chat online at loveisrespect.org. TTY users can call 1-866-331-8453. Services are available in English and Spanish, with access to interpreters in over 200 languages. All contact is free and confidential. Advocates understand how to protect your safety and privacy, especially important when an abusive partner may monitor communication.

sections.title: What love is respect Offers
sections.text: When you reach out to love is respect, trained peer advocates will help you explore your relationship concerns without judgment. Advocates can help with safety planning, understanding healthy vs. unhealthy relationship dynamics, learning your options, finding local resources and support services, and building confidence in making decisions. You don't have to be in immediate danger or certain that you're experiencing abuse—love is respect is here for questions and concerns of all kinds.

sections.title: Educational Resources
sections.text: The love is respect website offers extensive resources including quizzes to help you assess your relationship (Is My Relationship Healthy?), information about different types of abuse (emotional, physical, digital, financial, sexual), guides for helping a friend in an abusive relationship, and resources for understanding consent and boundaries. Materials are specifically designed for teens and young adults and cover topics like technology safety, supporting LGBTQ+ relationships, and recognizing gaslighting and manipulation.

sections.title: Supporting a Friend
sections.text: If you're worried about a friend's relationship, love is respect provides guidance on how to have supportive conversations and what to do if someone discloses abuse to you. Advocates can help you understand what your friend might be going through and how to be supportive without making decisions for them. Remember that leaving an abusive relationship can be dangerous and complicated, and the most helpful thing you can do is listen without judgment and let your friend know you care.
